defects: Hypothesis domain mismatch: gold's `h` universally quantifies only over *maximal* ideals m (comparing rankAtStalk at m to rankAtStalk at the fixed prime p), while produced's `hrank` universally quantifies over *all* prime ideals q : PrimeSpectrum R (asserting a single global constant n works for every prime, not just maximal ones). Since maximal ideals are a subset of primes, produced's hypothesis is strictly stronger than gold's — it is not a mere restatement but a genuine change in the class of ideals over which constancy is asserted.

The produced hypothesis ties rank-constancy to an existentially quantified global constant n independent of p, rather than to the value rankAtStalk M p as in gold; whether this reformulation is mathematically equivalent to gold's p-relative, maximal-ideals-only condition for general finite flat modules is not evident (and plausibly relies on exactly the kind of local-constancy fact this theorem is meant to help establish), so equivalence cannot be confirmed with confidence.
